name: walian-tem-cpt-sediment-wash-2021
description: Transmission electron microscopy of CPT sediment 'washes' by the Walian Lab (Peter Walian), used as a high-throughput means of imaging microbes in the 2020 cone penetrometer sediment samples (depth range 8-19 ft; water content from dry vadose to saturated; mostly clay-rich). Several extraction protocols were used, from gentle (lowest yield, best preservation of cell structure) to strong (higher yield, cell lysis and deformation). Findings (readme, 2021-09): few microbes observed regardless of protocol; most from push 21 (Mid-NW zone); the most common phenotype in Area 3 sediment is microbes with S-layers; Rhodanobacter among the more prominent non-S-layer microbes; no ultra-small cells or multi-cell clusters; maximum sediment AODC of ~10^6 cells/mL suggests about one cell per 100 um. Images are JPEG exports from the team Drive folder 'CPT EM imaging' (deck 'CPT EM imaging.pptx', readme 'Readme for CPT imaging.docx').

name: walian-als-832-microct-pilot-core-2017
description: X-ray micro-computed tomography of pilot sediment core sections (FW106 and EB271 cores, 2017) at the Advanced Light Source beamline 8.3.2, run by Peter Walian (Walian Lab), scanned and reconstructed on 2017-05-17. Each scan: 1,025 projections over 180 degrees on a 2560 x 2160 detector, reconstructed with tomopy (gridrec, Butterworth filter order 2 cutoff 0.25, phase-correlation rotation centre, nearest-flats normalisation, 1D outlier removal, Fourier-wavelet stripe removal (db5, level 8, sigma 4), edge padding, circular mask) by the beamline's dxchange pipeline; slices scaled by 1/6.38e-05 cm, i.e. a pixel size of 0.638 um (2560 pixels = 1.63 mm), written as 2,160 float32 TIFF slices of 2560 x 2560 per section, with the reconstruction script (.py) and parameter file (.yml) kept beside them. Fourteen reconstructions (FW106 sections 4-5, 5-5, 6-3, 6-5, 7-6, 8-5, 9-4, 10-1; EB271 sections 2-2, 3-3, 4-1, 4-4, 5-1, 5-2; 742 GB) were delivered to John-Marc Chandonia on a hard drive in December 2019; ten representative slices are on the team Drive.

name: walian-tem-groundwater-spring-2019
description: Transmission electron microscopy of unfiltered groundwater by the Walian Lab (Peter Walian; tallies by a student, 'Valerie results'): water from the Walian/Hazen R11 sample bottles of the Spring 2019 Integrated Sampling (GW821E background well, MLSB5 Area 2 multi-level sampler, FW100-20 Area 3) was concentrated onto EM grids, some grids stained with uranyl acetate ('UA') or treated with Mg or water washes, and imaged; microbes were tallied per grid window and classified as large cells (> 1 um), ultra-small cells (UMBs), phage and other morphotypes, and representative crops were filed by morphotype in the ENIGMA Image Atlas drive (ENIGMA_Imaging/Images_Groundwater). The MLSB6 groundwater of 2022-10-24 (one-off, unfiltered, imaged 2023-03-15) was examined the same way for ultra-small bacteria. Summary slides: 2019_Spring_Integrated Sampling/Walian Lab/GW imaging.pptx.
